docs.title: Deep Anomaly Detector
docs.text: Unsupervised anomaly detection on time-series sensor data using Isolation Forest and autoencoders.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Deep Anomaly Detector", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Sensor Data Generator: Creates synthetic time-series data for 4 sensors
  • pressure, temperature, flow_rate, vibration
  • Anomaly Injection: Adds spikes, drops, drifts, and noise anomalies at 5% ratio
  • Normal Data: Baseline sensor readings with realistic patterns
  • Dataset: 5000 timesteps, 4 sensors, window_size=30

docs.title: Simple Autoencoder (SimpleAutoencoder)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Neural network autoencoder (NumPy implementation)
  • Architecture: Input(120) → Hidden(64) → Encoding(16) → Hidden(64) → Output(120)
  • Input: Flattened 30-step windows of 4 sensors (30×4=120 features)
  • Training: Minimize reconstruction error on normal data
  • Detection: Anomaly if reconstruction error > threshold
  • Threshold: 95th percentile of training reconstruction errors
  • Epochs: 80, Learning Rate: 0.002, Batch Size: 64
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: SimpleLSTMPredictor (SimpleLSTMPredictor)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: LSTM-based next-step predictor (NumPy implementation)
  • Architecture: LSTM(input_dim=4, hidden_dim=32) → Dense(output_dim=4)
  • Input: Sequence of 30 timesteps of 4 sensors
  • Output: Predicted next timestep (4 values)
  • Training: Minimize prediction error on normal data
  • Detection: Anomaly if prediction error > threshold
  • Threshold: 95th percentile of training prediction errors
  • Epochs: 30, Learning Rate: 0.005
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: IsolationForestDetector (IsolationForestDetector)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Isolation Forest (scikit-learn)
  • Parameters: contamination=0.05, n_estimators=100
  • Input: Flattened 30-step windows
  • Output: Binary label (-1=anomaly, 1=normal) + anomaly score
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: SequenceProcessor
docs.text:
• Windowing: Creates sliding windows from time-series data
  • Normalization: Min-max normalization with fit/transform pattern
  • Parameters: window_size=30, stride=1

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask (Python)
  • Serialization: JSON request/response
  • Model Loading: Lazy loading from outputs/models/ on first request
  • Port: 5018

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (single page)
  • Visualization: Chart.js for sensor plots, detection results, forecasts
  • Style: Dark-themed responsive UI

docs.title: Anomaly Detection Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Generate / Input Sensor Data (n_points × 4 sensors)
   ↓
2. Create Sliding Windows (window_size=30)
   ↓
3. Flatten Windows (30×4 = 120 features)
   ↓
4. Model Detection
   ├── Autoencoder: reconstruction error > threshold → anomaly
   ├── Isolation Forest: predict → -1 = anomaly
   └── LSTM: prediction error > threshold → anomaly
   ↓
5. Results (labels, scores, metrics)
   ↓
6. Dashboard Visualization

docs.title: LSTM Forecasting Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Generate Normal Sensor Data
   ↓
2. Normalize
   ↓
3. Sliding Window (30 steps)
   ↓
4. LSTM predict_next(sequence) → predicted next values
   ↓
5. Compare predicted vs actual
   ↓
6. Forecast Results

docs.title: Model Comparison Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Generate Anomalous Dataset
   ↓
2. Create Windows + Flatten
   ↓
3. Run All Models on Same Data
   ↓
4. Compute TP, FP, FN, TN against true labels
   ↓
5. Calculate Precision, Recall, F1, Accuracy
   ↓
6. Comparison Results

version: '3.8'

    build: .

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn with multiple workers for production deployments
  • debug=False is already set in app.py
  • Configure proper logging for request/error tracking
  • Place behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Apache) for SSL termination
  • Models are lazy-loaded on first request - pre-train with train.py
  • Autoencoder and LSTM use NumPy implementations (no GPU required)
  • Memory usage scales with number of concurrent requests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Deep Anomaly Detector is an AI-based anomaly detection system for oil & gas sensor monitoring. It uses autoencoders, LSTM time-series forecasting, and Isolation Forest to detect anomalies in pressure, temperature, flow rate, and vibration sensor data.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd deep-anomaly-detector
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

Generates 5000 timesteps of synthetic sensor data and trains all three models (autoencoder, LSTM, Isolation Forest). Models are saved to outputs/models/.

docs.title: Start the API Server
docs.text:
python app.py

The server starts on http://localhost:5018.

docs.title: Open the Dashboard
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:5018 in your browser.

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text: python test_api.py

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Anomaly Detection: Run detection on generated sensor data with visual charts
  • LSTM Forecasting: See predicted vs actual sensor readings
  • Model Comparison: Compare precision, recall, F1, and accuracy across models
  • Model Statistics: View thresholds and training metadata

docs.title: Autoencoder
docs.text:
• Trained on normal sensor data only
  • High reconstruction error = anomaly
  • Threshold set at 95th percentile of normal data reconstruction errors

docs.title: LSTM Predictor
docs.text:
• Predicts next sensor reading from previous 30 timesteps
  • High prediction error = anomaly
  • Threshold set at 95th percentile of normal prediction errors

docs.title: Isolation Forest
docs.text:
• Unsupervised ensemble method
  • Isolates anomalies by random feature splits
  • Contamination parameter at 5%

docs.title: Using curl
docs.text:
Detect anomalies:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5018/api/detect \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"n_points": 500}'

Forecast sensor readings:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5018/api/forecast \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"n_points": 300}'

Compare models:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5018/api/compare \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"n_points": 500}'

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import requests

# Detect anomalies
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5018/api/detect", json={"n_points": 500})
data = response.json()
for model, det in data["detections"].items():
    print(f"{model}: {det['anomalies_detected']} anomalies detected")

# Forecast
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5018/api/forecast", json={"n_points": 300})
forecasts = response.json()["forecasts"]
print(f"Forecast steps: {len(forecasts)}")
print(f"First prediction: {forecasts[0]['predicted']}")

# Compare models
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5018/api/compare", json={"n_points": 500})
comparison = response.json()["comparison"]
for model, metrics in comparison.items():
    print(f"{model}: F1={metrics['f1_score']:.3f}, Precision={metrics['precision']:.3f}, Recall={metrics['recall']:.3f}")

docs.title: Using JavaScript
docs.text:
// Detect anomalies
const response = await fetch("http://localhost:5018/api/detect", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ n_points: 500 })
});
const data = await response.json();
Object.entries(data.detections).forEach(([model, det]) => {
  console.log(`${model}: ${det.anomalies_detected} anomalies`);
});

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
